Resolving typically involves log rotation, cleanup, or expanding storage, which requires coordination but not extensive architectural changes, placing the incident at a moderate level of operational complexity.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Verify write freeze before node reboot. Promote read-replica prior to primary teardown.

recurring_patterns.symptom_pattern: Disk usage /var/log exceeded 96% on host node-prod-4

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: No exact historical incidents for notification-hub disk usage; pattern suggests an emerging storage exhaustion issue requiring further root‑cause analysis.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
output.justification: The incident affects 45,000 users, far exceeding the 2,000‑user cross‑tier threshold defined in the SLA rule. remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Ensure the operator has the required root or ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us‑east‑1.
commands: kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep node-prod-4
verification: AWS identity matches ProdOperations role
kubectl context equals prod-us-east-1
node-prod-4 appears in the node list

remediation_steps.title: Assess Disk Utilization on Affected Node
remediation_steps.description: Collect precise disk usage metrics for /var/log on node-prod-4 and identify large log files that can be safely removed or rotated.
verification: df output shows usage < 80% after cleanup
No single log file exceeds 1 GB

remediation_steps.title: Perform Log Rotation and Cleanup
remediation_steps.description: Rotate existing logs, truncate oversized files, and delete stale archives older than 30 days to reclaim space.
verification: ssh ec2-user@node-prod-4 "df -h /var/log" shows usage reduced below 70%
No error messages returned from logrotate

remediation_steps.title: Cordon and Drain Node (if cleanup insufficient)
remediation_steps.description: If disk usage remains >80% after cleanup, safely evict pods from node-prod-4, add temporary storage, and reboot the node.
verification: kubectl get nodes | grep node-prod-4 shows SchedulingDisabled
All notification-hub pods are running on other nodes (READY=1/1)
After node returns, `kubectl uncordon node-prod-4` and verify node status Ready

remediation_steps.title: Promote Read‑Replica and Restart Primary Service
remediation_steps.description: Promote the standby notification‑hub database replica to primary, then restart the notification‑hub deployment to pick up the new storage state.
verification: RDS describe-db-clusters shows the replica now as Primary
kubectl get pods -l app=notification-hub shows all pods Ready
Application health endpoint returns 200

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks, verify log generation rates, and confirm user‑facing functionality.
commands: kubectl logs deployment/notification-hub --since=5m | grep -i panic || true
verification: Health endpoint returns {"status":"OK"}
No panic logs in the last 5 minutes
Alerting system shows zero active alerts for notification-hub

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert any changes made during remediation in reverse order, restoring original log files from backup, detaching added storage, and rolling back the deployment to its pre‑remediation image tag. Verify service health after each reversal step.

steps.title: Restore Truncated Logs (if needed)
steps.description: If log truncation caused loss of required data, restore from the most recent backup snapshot.
verification: ssh ec2-user@node-prod-4 "ls -l /var/log/notification-hub/" shows restored files
df -h /var/log shows usage consistent with pre‑remediation state

steps.title: Detach Added EBS Volume
steps.description: If a new EBS volume was attached to increase /var/log capacity, detach it and revert to original volume size.
verification: aws ec2 describe-volumes --volume-ids vol-0xyz1234abcd5678 shows state detached
Node disk usage returns to original level (< 96%)

steps.title: Rollback Deployment Image Tag
steps.description: Undo any rollout restart that may have pulled a new container image; revert to the previously stable tag.
verification: kubectl describe deployment notification-hub | grep Image shows previous tag
Pods report Ready status and health endpoint returns OK

steps.title: Demote Primary Database (if promotion occurred)
steps.description: If the read‑replica promotion is not desired, fail back to the original primary using a controlled switchover.
verification: RDS describe-db-clusters shows original primary restored
Application connectivity tests succeed

steps.title: Uncordon Node and Re‑schedule Pods
steps.description: If the node was cordoned and drained, bring it back into service and allow pods to reschedule.
commands: kubectl get pods -o wide | grep node-prod-4
verification: kubectl get nodes shows node-prod-4 Ready
Notification‑hub pods are evenly distributed and Ready

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified (root or ProdOperations SSO)
Recent backup of /var/log and database snapshots exist
safety_verification.notes: All steps are documented, reversible, and include verification checkpoints before proceeding to the next action.
